data.description:
## Observation
Outside the agent sandbox on 2026-11-20 at about 06:00 PST (host load average 25-45 from concurrent verifies), `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py::test_two_processes_publish_at_most_one_equivalent_same_ticket_bundle` failed 2 of 2 serial runs with `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError` from `future.result(timeout=60)` (test line 401), after 247 s and 203 s of wall time. Each of the 2 `ProcessPoolExecutor` workers starts a fresh interpreter, imports rebar, and commits a completion bundle through git.

Inside the sandbox the same test fails earlier for a different reason, filed as allstar-sleepy-armadillo.

## Hypothesis (unproven)
The 60 s per-future bound is a wall-clock assumption about worker start-up and git latency that a loaded host violates; it adds no hang protection beyond the suite's 300 s per-test budget, because leaving the `with ProcessPoolExecutor` block still waits for the workers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A deterministic reproduction (for example a git shim adding a fixed delay per start inside the workers) is recorded here.
- [ ] The test no longer depends on a hard-coded worker wall-clock bound, with the reproduction passing.
data.title: test_two_processes_publish_at_most_one_equivalent_same_ticket_bundle waits only 60 s for its worker processes
